title: What do we get when we add up the all ones sequence?
description: The all ones sequence is added up one step at a time, and then added up and down. Adding up gives the counting numbers, and adding up and down gives the odd numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the ones up for running totals, then add them up and down for totals that climb and fall back. Watch for students who count the turning one twice.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (Try This), p.8
video_script.why: The child builds running totals of the all ones sequence, then totals that climb and fall back, and names the sequences that come out.
video_script.substitution: The numbers are all ones instead of three, six, nine and twelve.
video_script.anchor: a row of ones, with brackets that group them into running totals
video_script.payoff_line: Adding up gives the counting numbers, and adding up and down gives the odd numbers

final_answer.value: up: 1, 2, 3, 4, ... the counting numbers; up and down: 1, 3, 5, 7, ... the odd numbers
final_answer.spoken: the counting numbers, and the odd numbers

maths_rules: adding up and down: 1, 1 + 1 + 1 = 3, 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5, seven ones = 7
the k-th up and down total has k ones going up and k - 1 coming down, so 2k - 1 ones
check: the third total is 3 + 2 = 5 ones, which is 5
video_script.design: A row of ones is grouped by brackets, first as growing running totals, then as groups that climb and fall back.

beats.on_screen: Answer: up gives the counting numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, ...; up and down gives the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, ...

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Adding up gives the counting numbers, and adding up and down gives the odd numbers. Both come from the same row of ones.
